# fortiappseccloud_waf_template_web_socket_security

Configures WebSocket security for one FortiAppSec Cloud WAF template using the static template endpoint `/waf/template/{template_id}/web_socket_security`. This resource owns the template's module settings. To make an application inherit them, configure the matching app module resource with `template = true` and omit its `configs` block.

Declare only one `fortiappseccloud_waf_template_web_socket_security` resource for a WAF template.

## Example Usage

```hcl
resource "fortiappseccloud_waf_template_web_socket_security" "example" {
  template_id = fortiappseccloud_waf_template.example.template_id

  configs {
    status = true
    action = "alert_deny"

    rule_list {
      item {
        name              = "ws-rule"
        url               = "/ws"
        allow_binary_text = true
        allow_plain_text  = true
        allow_websocket   = true
        block_attacks     = true
        block_extensions  = false
        max_frm_size      = 64
        max_msg_size      = 1024

        origin_list {
          item {
            origin = "https://example.com"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

- `template_id` (Required, Forces replacement) — WAF template ID.
- `configs` (Required) — Typed WebSocket security configuration. Its attributes and ownership-wrapper blocks are identical to `fortiappseccloud_waf_web_socket_security` when that app resource uses `template = false`.

## Import

Import using the template ID:

```shell
terraform import fortiappseccloud_waf_template_web_socket_security.example TEMPLATE_ID
```

The first read after import hydrates all supported ownership wrappers.

## Destroy Behavior
Destroy performs a fresh GET, preserves the complete response, sets `template=false` and `configs.status=false`, sends the complete PUT, and verifies the normalized GET response before Terraform removes the resource from state.
